STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white plate with a rim band and a flat centre, no inner wall visible. It is a flat square plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: square plates are 20-30 cm. The plate looks like a standard dinner-size square, so about 25 cm.
b) Reference cue: the green beans are about 6-8 cm long. The plate spans roughly 3.5 to 4 bean-lengths across the visible width (from x≈155 to x≈615 px, about 460 px). A bean is about 120-130 px long, so the plate is about 3.6 beans wide, roughly 25 cm if beans are ~7 cm.
Reconciled width: about 25 cm (square). Area = 25 x 25 = 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Green beans (cooked, sauteed): they form a loose heap roughly 12 cm x 8 cm in footprint, about 70% of that rectangle covered, so footprint ≈ 0.7 x 96 ≈ 67 cm². Thickness: beans stack about 2 deep at the thickest point (~1.5 cm), averaging about 0.8 cm. Volume ≈ 54 ml. Cooked green beans bulk density ~0.6 g/ml, so ≈ 32 g. Likely a bit more hidden underneath, so take about 40 g.
- Bacon (two to three strips, cooked, crisp): footprint roughly 15 cm x 6 cm of strips, ~40% covered ≈ 36 cm². Thickness ~0.4 cm (flat strips). Volume ≈ 14 ml, density ~1.0 g/ml, so ≈ 15 g. Cooked bacon is fatty, so keep about 15 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No base layer (no rice, sauce, or grains) is visible. The plate has a light surface with no pooled sauce, so no extra items.

STEP 5 - Energy per 100 g (as served):
- Cooked green beans, sauteed with a little oil: about 40 kcal/100 g (including small oil uptake, taken as ~45).
- Cooked bacon, pan-fried crisp: about 540 kcal/100 g.

Totals: beans 40 g × 0.45 ≈ 18 kcal; bacon 15 g × 5.4 ≈ 81 kcal. Total ≈ 100 kcal, about 55 g of food.
